records.completeOperativeProcedure:
NEW ACQ-05 purchase/bond distinction: acquire Animal Companion once by committing one actual earned unspent feat opportunity while meeting its actual Animal Handling proficiency prerequisite and all other acquisition gates. Record that paid grant and its acquisition snapshot atomically. The animal and bonding hour are not conditions of purchasing the feat. Ownership begins at that commitment, with no companion and one unspent bond attempt under FS-06; it grants neither an animal nor an earlier completed Long Rest. Animal identity, matching template and any actually sourced sense choice belong to each bond record, not a permanently locked feat-purchase choice. The retained nonrepeatability/permanent-choice metadata does not prohibit the replacements expressly allowed here. Canceling a proposed purchase before commitment spends no opportunity. A completed purchase is not refunded or repeated because no animal is available, a bond attempt fails, or a bond later ends. Animal Companion ownership alone can satisfy Companion Training's printed parent alternative, but supplies neither its separate feat opportunity nor a creature on which to use it.

NEW ACQ-05 bond attempt: an owner of this feat with actual Animal Handling proficiency, no current feat bond, no other pending bond attempt, an unspent attempt and any required post-bond-ending Long Rest may select one already real, positive-HP living, willing/tamed, noncorrupted Beast with INT<7 fitting one of the three finite templates. The selected animal must have no incompatible existing bond, including another Animal Companion or Ranger bond. Finding, buying or taming it still needs actual lawful access and its real willing/tamed relationship to this owner; no animal, stocked shop, consent or charm is supplied. Preserve its actual identity, ordinary profile, current/maximum HP, conditions, injuries, native movement, breathing, custody and required template choices. In one ordered start event, recheck admission, reserve this owner and animal for the work, spend the one attempt, and begin the hour. Merely proposing a target or rejecting it before that event does not spend an attempt; it never reverses a previously completed feat purchase. Starting costs no RP, second feat opportunity or universal fee. An attempt cannot begin while an existing feat bond is retained; such a rejected proposal does not release or alter that bond.

Spend one uninterrupted hour of actual bonding work together at touch range. Keep the same owner and animal, actual access, the required proficiency and animal eligibility throughout the work and at completion; the owner must remain able to perform it. This is active work, not beneficial rest, and grants no extra work Watch, assistant shortcut, handover or overlapping incompatible task. Loss of required touch-range access, willing/tamed eligibility, qualifying body state, or the owner's ability to continue, including incapacitation, or voluntary abandonment terminates the attempt. Elapsed time, real losses and the spent attempt persist; no partial hour, resumed fraction or same-epoch retry is awarded. The prospective animal remains in its actual current ordinary state; no feat profile or command entitlement was installed. After a full lawful hour, atomically complete the one bond and apply the existing template/HP conversion to the animal's latest lawful ordinary state, using the owner's then-current governing statistics. No new bond check or success chance is added. Admission alone or an incomplete hour cannot establish a companion.

The initial allowance is one attempt at feat purchase. Each genuinely completed beneficial owner Long Rest thereafter sets the allowance to one, never adds a stored second attempt. Apply FS-06's actual rest limits and one elapsed clock: no reset from Short Rest, debt-only Rest, a repeated rest receipt, a scene, a new target, a new controller, a new day label or level growth. Do not credit active bonding or release work as rest. An invalid claimed completion record is evidence rejection, not an attempt or feat-payment refund: reconcile the real start/interruption/rest history. Missing history cannot be replaced by an assumed unspent allowance. One feat bond at a time. Use the template corresponding to the real animal's body/native movement; do not turn a dog into a bird or grant a new breathing mode. AC12+floor(ownerPB/2), maximumHP5+total owner level; template attack/ability/movement values are explicit NEW. At initial bond convert existing HP proportionally max(1,floor(newMax×oldHP/oldMax)); preserve actual conditions/injuries. Later maximum growth never heals, decreases clamp without damage. Ordinary legal healing works, but no Hit Dice/rest-refill is invented. Use one shared BA command within60ft while the animal can perceive you: in its attached phase after your regular turn, move and make its one attack or Dash/Disengage/Help/Dodge. No independent turn/Reaction; uncommanded move defensively and Dodge. The animal's HP-only chassis dies at0, producing its one actual corpse and ending the bond, with no Wound/death-save sequence; this is a feat-specific NEW rule, not generic animal law. NEW ACQ-05 replacement boundary: when an established feat bond ends through release or death, record that actual ending event. Before this owner begins any later feat bond, require a genuinely beneficial owner Long Rest whose completion is ordered after that event, as well as an available attempt, a real eligible living target and the full new hour. A rest completed before the ending event or an unused prior allowance cannot satisfy that replacement gate. A qualifying completion after the event is sufficient; no additional rule requires the whole rest to have started after it. Existing active-work/rest restrictions still apply. Replacement is a use of the already-owned nonrepeatable feat, not a second purchase. NEW explicit rebond interpretation: a previously released living animal may be selected again if it genuinely qualifies; it is a new bond to the same physical individual, not a new or refreshed animal. A dead animal never becomes eligible merely through rest, release, purchase or this procedure. Voluntary release requires the owner's one uninterrupted hour of actual release work. NEW ACQ-05 release boundary: record its start, but end the bond only on lawful completion; interruption or abandonment grants no partial-hour credit and leaves the existing bond intact unless an independent event already ended it. A fresh release hour may be begun while the bond still exists. Release consumes no bond attempt, feat opportunity or RP. It does not require a second target or borrow the bonding hour's touch-range requirement; actual owner capacity and uninterrupted work remain mandatory. At completion restore the same living animal's saved ordinary profile with the existing positive-current-HP ratio conversion, preserving its current conditions, injuries and actual custody without healing or refilling it. End the outgoing bond's control entitlement and unexecuted commands; preserve all already-spent body/actor allowances. No automatic transfer of custody or command occurs. Record this end for the post-ending Long-Rest gate. A creature cannot simultaneously have this and a Ranger bond, or two owners' Animal Companion bonds. NEW ACQ-05 correction of 'new paid acquisition': a transfer requires the outgoing bond to end through its actual lawful release/death/termination procedure, real lawful access/custody for the receiver, and the receiver's independently authorized new bond. An existing Animal Companion feat owner does not buy that nonrepeatable feat again; they spend their own available attempt and full hour and satisfy their own post-ending Long-Rest gate, if any. The sender's rest, feat ownership or spent attempt neither transfers nor resets the receiver's history. A receiver without this feat must first acquire it through their own actual eligible unspent opportunity, or use an independently acquired receiving engine; receiving the animal grants no feat or class feature. An actual Ranger Beast Companion route retains its own acquired Warder/class-level/selection gates, eligible-beast limits, 4 RP, one-hour touch procedure, once-per-beneficial-owner-Long-Rest allowance and native profile/lifecycle. This feat's no-RP route, release hour and attempt rules do not waive or redefine that class engine. A Ranger bond cannot be ended by invoking another engine's feat-release permission. No universal transfer payment, new animal, healing, additive chassis, second controller, extra phase or refunded body/resource budget is granted. Owner death ends the bond and, if the animal remains alive, restores its saved ordinary profile using the same positive-HP ratio conversion as release; a dead animal remains its actual corpse. Temporary owner incapacity prevents new commands but does not cancel a previously committed legal command; after that command, uncommanded phases remain defensive. This never supplies autonomous attacks.
NEW explicit EX58 interface: retain one real creature identity and one current control/phase record. Riding, bonding or transferring custody does not clone a turn, movement budget, Reaction, attack allowance, body or resource pool. An attached companion acts in its source-defined phase after the owner’s regular turn; a controlled mount uses EX58’s actual mounted-phase procedure. A body fitting both roles elects one compatible route before that round’s work, preserves all already-spent allowances and cannot switch routes to gain a second phase. Its actual load, tack, rider geometry, mounting/dismounting cost and ordinary independent temperament remain. One shared Bonus Action command and one offensive companion action per owner per numbered round apply where those source engines impose them. This feat supplies no blanket override of a specific engine’s attack or no-resource restrictions.
The three supplied body templates are NEW complete feat chassis, not evidence that such a Beast is available. Use only the corresponding real body/native mode. Saved ordinary maximum/currentHP and original constituent identity are required before bonding; no missing oldHP record is replaced by invented full health. The feat’s0HP-death rule applies only to this feat chassis; an independently governed mount/Ranger chassis retains its own rules rather than taking both.

records.completeOperativeProcedure:
## Chef — General; no prerequisite

During an actual long-rest attempt, use cook's utensils and spend one uninterrupted hour cooking. This is permitted light activity only when the normal long-rest procedure permits that hour; the feat does not enlarge the allowance. Designate one batch of1..current PB intended servings at cooking start. Only one batch may be designated per rest attempt and only one can gain potency per successful completed rest.

On successful cooking completion, consume one real standard ration or meal-equivalent ingredient per intended serving. Create exactly that many physical prepared-food items, each with its own identity. Their food exists immediately, but they gain no feat potency before the rest actually succeeds. If the rest fails, the ingredients remain spent and the food remains ordinary. An incomplete cooking hour creates no special food.

At successful long-rest completion, first resolve old rest-expiring effects and advance the rest epoch. Then snapshot the Chef's current PB and empower up to `min(physically prepared servings still present, current PB)` items. Each grants `2 × PB at batch finalization` temporary HP. A PB increase cannot manufacture more ingredients or servings; a decrease leaves excess prepared items ordinary.

A creature with a legal serving must spend one uninterrupted minute eating it. Completing a legal offer consumes the serving and the recipient's **Chef-family entitlement for its current completed-long-rest epoch**, even if an equal/stronger existing grant wins. This limit is shared across every Chef. The Chef's own rest does not reset another recipient's entitlement.

Potency ends at the earlier of24 elapsed hours from successful batch creation or the Chef's next completed long rest after the creation rest. An already consumed/discarded item never returns. Expired potency leaves ordinary food, with no magical premium value. Potency expiration does not end a previously granted shield; that shield has the recipient's default lifetime.

Chef servings are distinct from crafted Feast recipes. Chef grants no recipe ingredients, crafting checks, RP restoration, creature traits or recipe power. It does not occupy the recipe system's one-feast-at-a-time slot. A lawful recipe rider can coexist with a Chef rider; temporary HP still do not stack. One physical meal cannot claim both effects unless an exact recipe expressly supports it. Recipe-specific ten-minute eating, longer crafting and materials remain independent.

**NEW:** the finite batch transaction, quantities, preparation/eating times, recipient-family cap, potency expiry and explicit no-duplication/economy bridges. The source's long-rest cooking role is preserved.

As a Bonus Action, use one actual healer's-kit use on one legally reachable living dying creature. Resolve the canonical automatic kit stabilization, including its normal1d4-hour recovery deadline. Different owners do not share an artificial family lock, but each must actually cause a valid transition. A new episode requires a genuine exit from the old dying episode and later entry into dying; damage absorbed entirely by temporary HP does not create one.

The later1HP does not erase the stabilization trigger. The feat itself provides no normal HP, consciousness, Wound removal or resurrection. No background is granted by acquiring this feat.

**NEW integration:** event/episode anti-replay identity and ordering with independent recovery; the broad “when you stabilize” trigger is preserved.

At that eligible cast’s commitment, declare two full placements of the same actual area geometry, each independently legal under the original casting range/origin/line rules. Both placements have full native size/effect; NEW a creature or physical target included by both is resolved only once for each actual native spell trigger event. Roll shared native damage once for the combined simultaneous application, then resolve each distinct target’s save/defenses. No overlapping double damage, duplicate save or control record. For sustained zones, keep one actual spell identity and its existing per-target trigger budget across both areas; moving through both cannot reset a same-turn/round/cast allowance. Later pulses occur at the original spell’s real deadlines, and a genuine different native trigger remains distinct only where the original card already permits it. Concentration loss or ordinary ending ends both. If the source allows one area-movement command, NEW move at most one placement with that one command, not both for free; each remains subject to all actual control ranges. A dispel selecting this single ongoing cast ends its whole duplicated area application unless the original spell explicitly defines independently separable effects. The feat adds no second spell, second payload budget or half-strength Echo Spell rule.

Separately identify rare/unique inputs before applying a discount to a mixed bill. No classification from absence: an unitemized ambiguous special-ink bill must be resolved by its source procedure before a discount is claimed. Level-up free additions remain free. Matrix preparation, reconstructing unknown text from memory, formula research and copying an ordinary craft formula are not spell/scroll copying. A usable scroll can be duplicated only under a separately authorized scroll-production procedure; the feat supplies no procedure or item effect.

FT84 source-follow-through selection (proposed; the following explicit interaction controls only this named composition):
FT84-Q01 / FT84-WRITTEN-RITUAL-01 — scoped selection for Ritual Caster learning and Spell Scribe.
INTERPRETATION SELECTED: the actual Ritual Caster written-learning route is an authorized spell-copying procedure when the learner personally uses an already complete, legitimately accessible written version of the exact eligible ritual, can actually use its language/notation, and records the learned ritual in the learner's real usable ritual book. This predicate is about how the real work is done; the presence of a tutor does not disqualify otherwise genuine written copying, and writing lecture notes does not convert teacher-led learning into copying.
For that written-copy work, an actually acquired Spell Scribe halves the ordinary eight-active-hours-per-rank learning requirement; take the strongest eligible time factor once, then apply Spell Scribe's final whole-minute upward rounding. A current rank-one ritual therefore requires 240 active minutes. Retain every completed 15-minute learning phase and its governing interruption/final-remainder rule. No reading, comprehension, recording, rank, tag, consent, facility, tool or source requirement disappears. Diligent Researcher, Craftsman, Quick Ritualist and Ritual Channeler do not reduce this learning transaction. No new starting ritual or physical book, Wizard spellbook entitlement, ordinary scroll-production permission, check, trade XP or automatic class acquisition is granted.
Teacher-led learning without the qualifying complete written source remains 480 active minutes per rank. A later lawful switch to written-copy work can affect only actually remaining unworked learning at a completed phase boundary; log the old and new basis and retain all actual time/materials. Do not retroactively relabel completed teaching or an interrupted uncredited segment as discounted copying. Only one route credits each actual minute. Wizard Spell Scribing keeps its own legal-found-Wizard-spell/spellbook predicate and its own bill; merely being a Wizard or having the same physical book does not substitute its class route for this feat route. When two reductions genuinely cover the same procedure and material category, take the strongest once, not their product.
NEW LIMITED BILL COMPLETION: before claiming a material reduction, record the real ten-gp-per-rank practice/writing bill as actual stock quantities and identified categories; it is not a new currency-only substitute for materials. Ordinary blank writing stock, ordinary nonrare ink and ordinary practice supplies are discountable only when their actual source/provider identifies them as such. Rare inks and unique or specifically required components remain full quantity; copying rights, instructor/facility services, reusable tools and the separate blank book are not made discountable by calling them consumables. There is no universal numeric split of the ten gp. A stated mixed bill must retain its undiscounted total and each actual lot's identity, availability and legal precision. Apply Spell Scribe's 3/4 mundane factor separately from time; preserve divisible quantities, ceil required indivisible units once, and ceil the final actual purchase once to copper. Known protected items remain unchanged.
An unitemized or ambiguous bill has no justified material discount. The otherwise legal learner may still use the qualifying half-time route and supply the complete genuine undiscounted materials/bill; missing classification does not ban copying or its independent time benefit. Missing actual required materials still prevents work. No guessed rarity classification, refund for supplies already used, duplication of the source, free rare ink or teaching-cost waiver follows. Real consumption, deterioration and fees are recorded as they occur; interruption loses only its actual phase credit and actual resources, never refills stock.

FEAT335-COPY-RELEASE-SOURCE-01-ADDENDUM — controlling release completion.
NEW feat-copy chronological identity. Every paid feat-copy cast records `castFamilyKey = feat-copy::<canonicalSourceEffectId>`. `canonicalSourceEffectId` is the stable identity of the actually witnessed underlying spell/effect from which the bounded profile was captured; for a source-qualified monster ability use that ability's stable source identity. Changing the capture event, owner, Eldritch Echo/Mimicry/Arcane Adaptation permission, bounded profile, selected damage/type component, q, or qualifying casting-ability route does not create a new family. Copies sharing that key use the ordinary chronological Refrain history together. An ordinary cast of the underlying spell uses its ordinary spell family and does not share the feat-copy family; Mirrorsage Echo Release likewise keeps its own class family. A missing stable underlying source identity is ineligible for release rather than being assigned a favorable new key. This key grants no ordinary spell knowledge or access.

NEW feat-copy concentration tags. Strike: no. Burst: no. Mend: no. Ward: yes. Hindrance: yes. Boon: yes. Step: no; its movement/teleport resolves instantaneously. A concentration-required copy establishes the releaser's one concentration burden during casting commitment under the ordinary sequence, ending an incompatible existing concentration before the counter window. If that cast is later countered, prior concentration remains ended and no copied lasting effect remains. Loss of concentration ends the Ward/Hindrance/Boon copied effect immediately; their printed earlier deadlines still cap duration. Immediate profiles establish no new concentration burden. Ready is separate: preparation already occupies concentration. On release, an immediate profile resolves and that Ready concentration ends with the released spell; a concentration-required Ward/Hindrance/Boon continues on that same one concentration burden, never a second slot. No witnessed original concentration tag is inherited or used to change these seven profile tags.

COPY-ROUTE STRAIN SCOPE. A paid feat-copy cast under FS-08 is an independent feat-casting route for strain purposes. Use FS-09 exactly: base Dissonance 0 for q/rank 0, 1 for ranks 1-5, and 2 for ranks 6-9; apply ordinary same-family Refrain using CRS-01; and use `Limit = max(4, 2*PB + casting modifier)` for that copy route, including its existing surcharge/block thresholds. The owned route chosen to qualify the copy supplies only the permitted casting ability, rank ceiling and other expressly required source credentials; it does not import that class engine's protected Dissonance reduction, routing, vent, prepared-matrix treatment or proc chain into the feat-copy cast. In particular a Wizard-qualified copy is not a prepared matrix, a Shaman-qualified copy is not an ordinary Shaman spell for the totem vent, and a Mirrorsage-qualified copy is not class Echo Release. The ordinary `max(4, 2 + PB + max(0, modifier))` Limit in SPELL_INTEGRATION_RULES remains controlling for ordinary class spells within its existing scope and is not globally changed here. If the only qualifying route is the feat-only Eldritch Blast grant, it supplies CHA and only its actual rank-0 ceiling; it does not change the copy engine or Limit, create a Warlock/class engine, or qualify a ranked q>0 copy.

COPY-READY-ALLOWANCE-02 — owner-directed preparation-round-only successor for the seven FS-08/SUP-07 feat-copy profiles used through Arcane Adaptation, Eldritch Echo and Mimicry. This supersedes COPY-READY-ALLOWANCE-01's both-touched-round policy only. All earlier archives and receipts retain their exact historical wording. This selection changes no profile payload, acquisition predicate, ordinary Ready rule, ordinary class casting cadence or unrelated Mirrorsage class Echo procedure.

PREPARATION. The shared feat-copy cap counts new paid feat-copy casting commitments: a direct cast commits in its current numbered round; a Readied feat copy commits in its preparation numbered round. Require and atomically spend that round's owner feat-copy allowance. If the owner actually has the separately acquired Mirrorsage shared-release engine to which the exact source binds this feat copy, also require and spend that same preparation round's actual shared class allowance. A qualifying ability route alone never creates that engine. Validate the actual setup prerequisites first. At legal preparation commitment, pay the Action, current quote and other actual costs, consume the applicable permission/use once, provide components, record the independent feat-copy family/Dissonance/Refrain once, and establish the one Ready concentration burden before its single preparation counter window. No partial class/feat/resource debit is allowed. Countering, abandonment, replacement, expiry or concentration loss after commitment never refunds those preparation spends, recreates a capture, restores displaced concentration or reopens that round's allowance. Failed precommit validation spends nothing and cannot delete an existing valid hold.

HELD RECORD. Bind one unique preparation ID and actual owner to its fixed captured source/profile/q/mode, preparation-bound choices, paid transaction, consumed permission receipt, preparation round and actual ledger identities. Preserve its original Ready deadline and every independently applicable earlier source/capture/use deadline. Consuming the capture permission at preparation is not itself loss of this paid hold's authorization, but the hold cannot extend the original permission window. No future round's allowance is reserved. The hold remains subject to ordinary concentration, body/source availability and valid replacement rules. Paid preparation alone creates no payload. Earlier prose calling the limit one-copy-release per round is controlled here: it limits new direct casts and Ready preparations, not a later completion of this same paid hold.

RELEASE. After an actual perceivable trigger has completed and before every governing deadline, validate the actual hold and its preparation receipts, the available lawful Reaction, continuing concentration and the release predicates at the points required by their actual sources. Select legal current targets/ordered recipients/area/destination at release under the fixed preparation profile and mode; do not freeze a setup-time ghost target or rewrite preparation-bound choices from hidden results. Neither same-round nor later-round release checks, reserves or spends a new feat-copy allowance or a new Mirrorsage shared-release allowance. The preparation receipts remain spent in their original round. An otherwise lawful delayed release therefore remains eligible even when the release round's feat allowance, an actually owned class shared allowance, or both have already been spent by another lawful use. This exemption belongs only to completion of that specific paid feat-copy hold; it does not waive any new direct cast's or unrelated class Echo's own allowances.

A declined trigger or an invalid precommit release, including no actual Reaction, invalid target/geometry, missing source predicate or uncompleted/unperceived trigger, spends no Reaction, makes no new debit and grants no hidden diagnostic. Keep the existing hold only while its actual concentration and original deadlines permit; another genuine trigger occurrence may be considered. An already-spent release-round copy allowance alone is NOT a failed-release reason. At an exact governing expiry, expiry wins. Lost concentration, actual abandonment, successful replacement or another real ending terminates the hold without a refund; a failed release cannot restore a hold that ended.

On a valid release commitment, atomically consume this hold once and spend the real Reaction before resolving its one payload. No second RP/material payment, capture-use consumption, casting-family/Refrain update, cast hook or Counterspell window occurs. Subsequent prevention or a failed attack/save outcome does not refund the Reaction or preparation; actual source-specific hidden-eligibility checks retain their own paid timing. Duplicate callbacks/retry IDs cannot create a second payload or debit. Immediate Strike/Burst/Mend/Step end the held concentration after resolution. Ward/Hindrance/Boon continue the same one burden under their actual effect clock and earlier limits, never a second concentration slot.

OTHER USES AND PERSISTENCE. Another copy in the release round still needs its own genuinely available Action/source permission, current legal resources/credentials, its own new-commitment allowances and all ordinary concentration/cadence predicates. No Action, Reaction refresh, capture or second concentration slot is granted. A concentration-breaking new cast can end the old hold even though its allowance is irrelevant to the old release. Releasing a prior hold first leaves a genuinely free current-round allowance available for a separate lawful new commitment; a lawful prior current-round use does not by itself block the old hold's release. Actual competing-use opportunities before the owner's next regular START are illustrative prerequisites unless supplied by a real source; the old Ready cannot be carried past that START merely to obtain the ordinary Action. Save/load, extra turns, changing routes/profiles or round labels must preserve owner/hold identity, original expiry, actual consumed receipts, completed release identity and chronological/per-round ledgers. Release never rewrites a later cast's history. This rule is a proposed authoring successor, not implementation of scheduling, live perception, source-qualified recipient effects, canonical persistence or the game engine.

## Blood Ritual — Magic; Constitution13+ and character level4+

Perform a ten-minute ritual once per completed long rest. Commit the use at ritual start. Snapshot your character level, PB and selected targets then: yourself plus up to PB **other** willing allies. Each ally must remain within10ft throughout, witness the ritual and voluntarily contribute a drop of blood. There is no normal-HP payment. No substitutions are allowed after starting.

Each continuously eligible selected ally receives `snapshotted character level` temporary HP for one elapsed hour. A departed/ineligible ally loses only its own benefit. Your interruption fails the whole unfinished ritual and the use remains spent until a real rest resets it.

You also gain advantage on your next actual saving throw against an effect explicitly classified as a curse or disease. This rider is independent of the shield: rejection, replacement or depletion of temporary HP does not remove it. It ends when you roll that qualifying save or complete your next long rest, whichever is first. Consume it on the roll even if advantage cancels disadvantage or the save fails. It neither cures nor waives Oracle's intrinsic Curse and grants no oath or transformation.

If completion is strictly before a long-rest endpoint, the self shield/rider expire at that rest normally. At an exact tied completion, resolve old rest expirations, advance the epoch/reset resources, finalize Chef if applicable, then complete the tied ritual; its new shield/rider belong to the new epoch. Its already-committed start use is never retroactively refunded.

FEAT335-FLORA-SOURCE-CHECK-01 / FLQ-04 — NEW split command/phase completion. On the owner's regular turn, first establish a legal shared Bonus Action, an available owner/numbered-round offensive-companion allowance, and actual receipt of the required within-60-ft audible or visible command by each nominated participating plant. At that legal commitment spend the Bonus Action and that one shared offensive allowance once; record the owner, original regular-turn/round identity, participating plant IDs, one chosen mode and target or area, its permitted origin or nominated Lash origins, and the immediately following attached phase. This is a paid pending command, not a Readied action, independent plant turn or extra allowance. It need not be the owner's last voluntary decision that turn. Resolve it once in the attached phase after that same regular turn's actual end processing, using the preserved schedule; an extra turn neither advances nor duplicates that phase. Recheck the surviving unended, unsuppressed, otherwise capable participating plant and the mode's actual target/area, range, perception and line-of-effect requirements. For Lash, an independently legal surviving nominated origin may support the same selected target; losing the selected Spore/Entangle origin does not authorize another origin or mode. For an area, resolve its actual occupants at that phase. If the chosen outcome is no longer legal, close the pending command with no effect, no refund, no new target and no carry to a later phase. After actual receipt, later owner incapacity, Silence, loss of owner-to-plant sight/range/channel, or owner death alone does not retract that command: no continuous concentration/channel/consciousness requirement is added. These states can prevent a NEW command or personal creation/Bloom Burst. An effect expressly cancelling the pending command or disabling/ending its plant still controls. Once committed, no other companion or armed trap can spend the same owner-round allowance, and the phase does not spend it a second time.
KEEP the already-operative SUP-07 floraBody/dc acquisition requirement: at acquisition permanently select and record one actual possessed spellcasting route as this feat's DC provider. Use DC 8 + current PB + that route's current casting-ability modifier; do not invent Wisdom, Spellcraft or another default. This source choice is separate from the later seedling mode/burst-type choice. Ownership initializes only the finite creation allowance and body capacity, with no plant, pending additional creation, command or active effect. All printed acquisition predicates and the actual earned feat opportunity remain required.
FEAT335-FLORA-SOURCE-CHECK-01 / FLQ-01 — KEEP acquisition-only provider selection. A valid paid Conjure Flora acquisition permanently binds its actual qualifying personal casting route and the ability operand supplied by that route. Later loss, expiry, retraining-away or temporary unavailability of that casting grant does not by itself remove Conjure Flora, reselect its provider, prohibit an otherwise legal Flora creation/command/Bloom Burst, terminate an existing seedling or disable an already armed entry trap. Current prepared repertoire, renewable casting charges and RP are not new ongoing Flora prerequisites. This does not qualify a NEW feat acquisition through a grant that is actually gone; ACQ-03 still governs that separate snapshot. Flora is a magical nonspell feat, not a cast through the provider: a spell-only prohibition applies only to its actual scope, Silence still blocks an audible command, and an effect actually suppressing this feat, a plant, its magic or the required action applies under that effect's own rule. NEW explicit lost-provider representation: retain the original provider/ability binding and compute Flora DC as 8 + the owner's current lawful PB + the current modifier of that bound ability; no alternative route, Wisdom default, reconstructed casting entitlement or favorable old ability score is substituted. A missing or invalid original acquisition/provider record is not cured by this rule. Completed results are not recalculated, and existing body HP/save snapshots, deadlines, spent uses and ownership are not reset.
FEAT335-FLORA-SOURCE-CHECK-01 / FLQ-02–03 — NEW second-creation window completion. Each legally completed first creation records one original use ID, its first-plant ID and that plant's original minute deadline, with at most one additional creation unspent. This is a bounded open-use record even when the owner is below total level 10; it is not another rest use or an immediately usable creation at that level. Admit a second creation only while that same first plant remains present and unended, before its original deadline, with the additional creation unspent, current total character level at least 10, actual free plant capacity, and every ordinary Action, ground, range, line-of-effect and use predicate satisfied. The level-10 condition is live at the additional Action, not snapshotted at first creation. Genuine advancement during that open window can make the existing unspent permission usable, but creates no body, charge, healing or new window. Destruction, uprooting, Bloom Burst consumption, expiry or another actual ending of the first plant permanently closes any unused additional-creation permission immediately; its old future deadline does not keep that permission alive. Suppression without an actual ending is not by itself an ending. A legal additional creation consumes that one permission and costs its own Action, but no second rest use; its own minute begins at its own creation. Once the second plant exists, ending the first does not shorten the second's independent deadline. No ended plant, spent permission, missed deadline, level change, recovery, new ID or subsequent body can reopen the old use. A later beneficial rest restores only the ordinary creation allowance under FS-06; a later first creation starts a genuinely new use.
FEAT335-FLORA-SOURCE-CHECK-01 / FLQ-04 — NEW explicit owner/instance continuity. These particular one-minute, nonconcentration Flora bodies do not end merely because their owner is incapacitated or dies; retain the same owner, mode, actual body state, original deadline and no-resource restrictions. No recipient, ally, host, companion or replacement actor inherits control. A received pending command may resolve only at its already attached original phase under the split-command rule, even if the owner's live initiative slot is removed; preserve that one scheduled phase, not a new recurring independent turn. An already armed Trapcasting plant may perform its specified first-eligible-entry exception without a new owner Action/Reaction or remote command channel, even while its owner cannot act or is dead, but it still needs the actual qualifying entry, operative plant/trap, target legality and unspent same-owner numbered-round allowance. Incapacity/death neither refreshes that allowance nor rearms or moves the trap. Preserve the owner's last lawful PB/selected-ability state when its live actor view ends, applying any subsequently due source-defined changes; death is not a zero ability score, a new provider or a freeze of expiring modifiers. Use that continuing lawful record for later Flora DCs; a missing authoritative operand is an invalid/unestablished input, not permission to invent one. Lawful recovery continues the same history without replaying missed phases or refilling anything. Ending a generating plant still ends its own Poisoned/Restrained records immediately. A legally committed Bloom Burst binds its existing DC/type/area event, consumes its body before its one payload, and does not fail merely because that required consumption has occurred; it grants no other action to the ended body. Other independently applicable cancellation, suppression, condition, duration and target rules retain their own actual scope. No Animal Companion release/death rule or standard-companion movement/Dodge/attack is imported into these fixed Flora profiles.

FEAT335-COPY-RELEASE-SOURCE-01-ADDENDUM — controlling release completion.
NEW feat-copy chronological identity. Every paid feat-copy cast records `castFamilyKey = feat-copy::<canonicalSourceEffectId>`. `canonicalSourceEffectId` is the stable identity of the actually witnessed underlying spell/effect from which the bounded profile was captured; for a source-qualified monster ability use that ability's stable source identity. Changing the capture event, owner, Eldritch Echo/Mimicry/Arcane Adaptation permission, bounded profile, selected damage/type component, q, or qualifying casting-ability route does not create a new family. Copies sharing that key use the ordinary chronological Refrain history together. An ordinary cast of the underlying spell uses its ordinary spell family and does not share the feat-copy family; Mirrorsage Echo Release likewise keeps its own class family. A missing stable underlying source identity is ineligible for release rather than being assigned a favorable new key. This key grants no ordinary spell knowledge or access.

NEW feat-copy concentration tags. Strike: no. Burst: no. Mend: no. Ward: yes. Hindrance: yes. Boon: yes. Step: no; its movement/teleport resolves instantaneously. A concentration-required copy establishes the releaser's one concentration burden during casting commitment under the ordinary sequence, ending an incompatible existing concentration before the counter window. If that cast is later countered, prior concentration remains ended and no copied lasting effect remains. Loss of concentration ends the Ward/Hindrance/Boon copied effect immediately; their printed earlier deadlines still cap duration. Immediate profiles establish no new concentration burden. Ready is separate: preparation already occupies concentration. On release, an immediate profile resolves and that Ready concentration ends with the released spell; a concentration-required Ward/Hindrance/Boon continues on that same one concentration burden, never a second slot. No witnessed original concentration tag is inherited or used to change these seven profile tags.

COPY-ROUTE STRAIN SCOPE. A paid feat-copy cast under FS-08 is an independent feat-casting route for strain purposes. Use FS-09 exactly: base Dissonance 0 for q/rank 0, 1 for ranks 1-5, and 2 for ranks 6-9; apply ordinary same-family Refrain using CRS-01; and use `Limit = max(4, 2*PB + casting modifier)` for that copy route, including its existing surcharge/block thresholds. The owned route chosen to qualify the copy supplies only the permitted casting ability, rank ceiling and other expressly required source credentials; it does not import that class engine's protected Dissonance reduction, routing, vent, prepared-matrix treatment or proc chain into the feat-copy cast. In particular a Wizard-qualified copy is not a prepared matrix, a Shaman-qualified copy is not an ordinary Shaman spell for the totem vent, and a Mirrorsage-qualified copy is not class Echo Release. The ordinary `max(4, 2 + PB + max(0, modifier))` Limit in SPELL_INTEGRATION_RULES remains controlling for ordinary class spells within its existing scope and is not globally changed here. If the only qualifying route is the feat-only Eldritch Blast grant, it supplies CHA and only its actual rank-0 ceiling; it does not change the copy engine or Limit, create a Warlock/class engine, or qualify a ranked q>0 copy.

COPY-READY-ALLOWANCE-02 — owner-directed preparation-round-only successor for the seven FS-08/SUP-07 feat-copy profiles used through Arcane Adaptation, Eldritch Echo and Mimicry. This supersedes COPY-READY-ALLOWANCE-01's both-touched-round policy only. All earlier archives and receipts retain their exact historical wording. This selection changes no profile payload, acquisition predicate, ordinary Ready rule, ordinary class casting cadence or unrelated Mirrorsage class Echo procedure.

PREPARATION. The shared feat-copy cap counts new paid feat-copy casting commitments: a direct cast commits in its current numbered round; a Readied feat copy commits in its preparation numbered round. Require and atomically spend that round's owner feat-copy allowance. If the owner actually has the separately acquired Mirrorsage shared-release engine to which the exact source binds this feat copy, also require and spend that same preparation round's actual shared class allowance. A qualifying ability route alone never creates that engine. Validate the actual setup prerequisites first. At legal preparation commitment, pay the Action, current quote and other actual costs, consume the applicable permission/use once, provide components, record the independent feat-copy family/Dissonance/Refrain once, and establish the one Ready concentration burden before its single preparation counter window. No partial class/feat/resource debit is allowed. Countering, abandonment, replacement, expiry or concentration loss after commitment never refunds those preparation spends, recreates a capture, restores displaced concentration or reopens that round's allowance. Failed precommit validation spends nothing and cannot delete an existing valid hold.

HELD RECORD. Bind one unique preparation ID and actual owner to its fixed captured source/profile/q/mode, preparation-bound choices, paid transaction, consumed permission receipt, preparation round and actual ledger identities. Preserve its original Ready deadline and every independently applicable earlier source/capture/use deadline. Consuming the capture permission at preparation is not itself loss of this paid hold's authorization, but the hold cannot extend the original permission window. No future round's allowance is reserved. The hold remains subject to ordinary concentration, body/source availability and valid replacement rules. Paid preparation alone creates no payload. Earlier prose calling the limit one-copy-release per round is controlled here: it limits new direct casts and Ready preparations, not a later completion of this same paid hold.

RELEASE. After an actual perceivable trigger has completed and before every governing deadline, validate the actual hold and its preparation receipts, the available lawful Reaction, continuing concentration and the release predicates at the points required by their actual sources. Select legal current targets/ordered recipients/area/destination at release under the fixed preparation profile and mode; do not freeze a setup-time ghost target or rewrite preparation-bound choices from hidden results. Neither same-round nor later-round release checks, reserves or spends a new feat-copy allowance or a new Mirrorsage shared-release allowance. The preparation receipts remain spent in their original round. An otherwise lawful delayed release therefore remains eligible even when the release round's feat allowance, an actually owned class shared allowance, or both have already been spent by another lawful use. This exemption belongs only to completion of that specific paid feat-copy hold; it does not waive any new direct cast's or unrelated class Echo's own allowances.

A declined trigger or an invalid precommit release, including no actual Reaction, invalid target/geometry, missing source predicate or uncompleted/unperceived trigger, spends no Reaction, makes no new debit and grants no hidden diagnostic. Keep the existing hold only while its actual concentration and original deadlines permit; another genuine trigger occurrence may be considered. An already-spent release-round copy allowance alone is NOT a failed-release reason. At an exact governing expiry, expiry wins. Lost concentration, actual abandonment, successful replacement or another real ending terminates the hold without a refund; a failed release cannot restore a hold that ended.

On a valid release commitment, atomically consume this hold once and spend the real Reaction before resolving its one payload. No second RP/material payment, capture-use consumption, casting-family/Refrain update, cast hook or Counterspell window occurs. Subsequent prevention or a failed attack/save outcome does not refund the Reaction or preparation; actual source-specific hidden-eligibility checks retain their own paid timing. Duplicate callbacks/retry IDs cannot create a second payload or debit. Immediate Strike/Burst/Mend/Step end the held concentration after resolution. Ward/Hindrance/Boon continue the same one burden under their actual effect clock and earlier limits, never a second concentration slot.

OTHER USES AND PERSISTENCE. Another copy in the release round still needs its own genuinely available Action/source permission, current legal resources/credentials, its own new-commitment allowances and all ordinary concentration/cadence predicates. No Action, Reaction refresh, capture or second concentration slot is granted. A concentration-breaking new cast can end the old hold even though its allowance is irrelevant to the old release. Releasing a prior hold first leaves a genuinely free current-round allowance available for a separate lawful new commitment; a lawful prior current-round use does not by itself block the old hold's release. Actual competing-use opportunities before the owner's next regular START are illustrative prerequisites unless supplied by a real source; the old Ready cannot be carried past that START merely to obtain the ordinary Action. Save/load, extra turns, changing routes/profiles or round labels must preserve owner/hold identity, original expiry, actual consumed receipts, completed release identity and chronological/per-round ledgers. Release never rewrites a later cast's history. This rule is a proposed authoring successor, not implementation of scheduling, live perception, source-qualified recipient effects, canonical persistence or the game engine.

records.completeOperativeProcedure:
## Lifeleech — Magic; actual spellcasting ability

Before your spell's damage resolves, designate one eligible hostile target for that spell root and canonical round/window. Your first positive actual necrotic damage to that target in the window commits the entitlement, even if the eventual healing is0, prohibited, capped or unfunded. No retargeting after observing results; area spells do not harvest a separate heal from every target. The same continuing spell can qualify again in a later real round/window.

Raw self-healing is `floor(actual necrotic damage dealt /2)`. Use only the actual necrotic component, including actual temporary-HP absorption and normal HP lost under the existing actual-damage interface; no overkill. Targets must be genuine hostile opposition, not friendly/staged/trivial sacrifices or owner/ally-generated farming bodies. Natural attacks, Agony Lance and the Necrotic Affinity die alone are not spells. The feat removes no Wounds and cannot resurrect its dead owner.

**NEW finite resource — Lifeleech Recovery Reserve:** newly acquiring the feat starts at0. At each actual completed long rest set its capacity and remaining points to `2 × current character level`, snapshotted then. Level/PB changes between rests do not refill/recompute it. This reserve is neither RP nor Mutation Recovery Reserve. Persistent save imports must preserve validated spent state.

Run the ordinary two-pass healing modifiers/reductions/prohibitions. Preview uses available reserve to determine whether conditional bonuses requiring positive actual HP restoration qualify. Apply reductions before funding. Cap final legal healing potential by remaining reserve; spend that **entire funded amount** on commitment, including funded excess. All lawful healing bonuses consume this same reserve. Then restore HP subject to ordinary maximum HP and Critical ceiling, and calculate `genuine excess = max(0, funded amount − ordinary missing HP)`.

A broad HP-gain prohibition produces0 legal amount, spends0 reserve and creates0 excess. At reserve0 the round/root trigger still commits, but it produces neither restoration nor excess. Full HP can produce funded excess, but does not enable conditional bonuses requiring actual HP restoration. Critical's ceiling does not itself turn all unrestored points into excess.

Lifeleech provides no intrinsic excess converter. A separately authorized converter must have its own eligibility/cost/cadence/cap and consume each funded excess point once. An explicitly legal resource-output converter remains possible; incidental heal-triggered resource production is blocked. The child heal carries `noLifeleechRetrigger`, `blockHealCopyTriggers` and `blockResourceTriggers`; propagate these to downstream callers. The resource flag blocks incidental triggers, not an exact, separately paid excess-conversion transaction. No new resource converter is granted here.

Lifeleech also automatically collects one Soul Charge at an eligible hostile soul-bearing creature's actual death within30ft, perceived with legal line of effect. No crystal is required for Lifeleech's own collection. Use the shared resource/death rules below. Lifeleech alone cannot spend charges through abilities from the unowned Soul Cage feat.

It is not a resource-free nonspell release. It grants no ordinary repertoire/class feature or further capture, echo, reflection, external feat amplification, class resource/proc or reward chain. The concrete copy profile and its independent component/range/target/deadline limits still apply. This is deliberately different from Echo Spell/Twin Cast secondary results and from an actual Mirrorsage class Echo Release.

FEAT335-COPY-RELEASE-SOURCE-01-ADDENDUM — controlling release completion.
NEW feat-copy chronological identity. Every paid feat-copy cast records `castFamilyKey = feat-copy::<canonicalSourceEffectId>`. `canonicalSourceEffectId` is the stable identity of the actually witnessed underlying spell/effect from which the bounded profile was captured; for a source-qualified monster ability use that ability's stable source identity. Changing the capture event, owner, Eldritch Echo/Mimicry/Arcane Adaptation permission, bounded profile, selected damage/type component, q, or qualifying casting-ability route does not create a new family. Copies sharing that key use the ordinary chronological Refrain history together. An ordinary cast of the underlying spell uses its ordinary spell family and does not share the feat-copy family; Mirrorsage Echo Release likewise keeps its own class family. A missing stable underlying source identity is ineligible for release rather than being assigned a favorable new key. This key grants no ordinary spell knowledge or access.

NEW feat-copy concentration tags. Strike: no. Burst: no. Mend: no. Ward: yes. Hindrance: yes. Boon: yes. Step: no; its movement/teleport resolves instantaneously. A concentration-required copy establishes the releaser's one concentration burden during casting commitment under the ordinary sequence, ending an incompatible existing concentration before the counter window. If that cast is later countered, prior concentration remains ended and no copied lasting effect remains. Loss of concentration ends the Ward/Hindrance/Boon copied effect immediately; their printed earlier deadlines still cap duration. Immediate profiles establish no new concentration burden. Ready is separate: preparation already occupies concentration. On release, an immediate profile resolves and that Ready concentration ends with the released spell; a concentration-required Ward/Hindrance/Boon continues on that same one concentration burden, never a second slot. No witnessed original concentration tag is inherited or used to change these seven profile tags.

COPY-ROUTE STRAIN SCOPE. A paid feat-copy cast under FS-08 is an independent feat-casting route for strain purposes. Use FS-09 exactly: base Dissonance 0 for q/rank 0, 1 for ranks 1-5, and 2 for ranks 6-9; apply ordinary same-family Refrain using CRS-01; and use `Limit = max(4, 2*PB + casting modifier)` for that copy route, including its existing surcharge/block thresholds. The owned route chosen to qualify the copy supplies only the permitted casting ability, rank ceiling and other expressly required source credentials; it does not import that class engine's protected Dissonance reduction, routing, vent, prepared-matrix treatment or proc chain into the feat-copy cast. In particular a Wizard-qualified copy is not a prepared matrix, a Shaman-qualified copy is not an ordinary Shaman spell for the totem vent, and a Mirrorsage-qualified copy is not class Echo Release. The ordinary `max(4, 2 + PB + max(0, modifier))` Limit in SPELL_INTEGRATION_RULES remains controlling for ordinary class spells within its existing scope and is not globally changed here. If the only qualifying route is the feat-only Eldritch Blast grant, it supplies CHA and only its actual rank-0 ceiling; it does not change the copy engine or Limit, create a Warlock/class engine, or qualify a ranked q>0 copy.

COPY-READY-ALLOWANCE-02 — owner-directed preparation-round-only successor for the seven FS-08/SUP-07 feat-copy profiles used through Arcane Adaptation, Eldritch Echo and Mimicry. This supersedes COPY-READY-ALLOWANCE-01's both-touched-round policy only. All earlier archives and receipts retain their exact historical wording. This selection changes no profile payload, acquisition predicate, ordinary Ready rule, ordinary class casting cadence or unrelated Mirrorsage class Echo procedure.

PREPARATION. The shared feat-copy cap counts new paid feat-copy casting commitments: a direct cast commits in its current numbered round; a Readied feat copy commits in its preparation numbered round. Require and atomically spend that round's owner feat-copy allowance. If the owner actually has the separately acquired Mirrorsage shared-release engine to which the exact source binds this feat copy, also require and spend that same preparation round's actual shared class allowance. A qualifying ability route alone never creates that engine. Validate the actual setup prerequisites first. At legal preparation commitment, pay the Action, current quote and other actual costs, consume the applicable permission/use once, provide components, record the independent feat-copy family/Dissonance/Refrain once, and establish the one Ready concentration burden before its single preparation counter window. No partial class/feat/resource debit is allowed. Countering, abandonment, replacement, expiry or concentration loss after commitment never refunds those preparation spends, recreates a capture, restores displaced concentration or reopens that round's allowance. Failed precommit validation spends nothing and cannot delete an existing valid hold.

HELD RECORD. Bind one unique preparation ID and actual owner to its fixed captured source/profile/q/mode, preparation-bound choices, paid transaction, consumed permission receipt, preparation round and actual ledger identities. Preserve its original Ready deadline and every independently applicable earlier source/capture/use deadline. Consuming the capture permission at preparation is not itself loss of this paid hold's authorization, but the hold cannot extend the original permission window. No future round's allowance is reserved. The hold remains subject to ordinary concentration, body/source availability and valid replacement rules. Paid preparation alone creates no payload. Earlier prose calling the limit one-copy-release per round is controlled here: it limits new direct casts and Ready preparations, not a later completion of this same paid hold.

RELEASE. After an actual perceivable trigger has completed and before every governing deadline, validate the actual hold and its preparation receipts, the available lawful Reaction, continuing concentration and the release predicates at the points required by their actual sources. Select legal current targets/ordered recipients/area/destination at release under the fixed preparation profile and mode; do not freeze a setup-time ghost target or rewrite preparation-bound choices from hidden results. Neither same-round nor later-round release checks, reserves or spends a new feat-copy allowance or a new Mirrorsage shared-release allowance. The preparation receipts remain spent in their original round. An otherwise lawful delayed release therefore remains eligible even when the release round's feat allowance, an actually owned class shared allowance, or both have already been spent by another lawful use. This exemption belongs only to completion of that specific paid feat-copy hold; it does not waive any new direct cast's or unrelated class Echo's own allowances.

A declined trigger or an invalid precommit release, including no actual Reaction, invalid target/geometry, missing source predicate or uncompleted/unperceived trigger, spends no Reaction, makes no new debit and grants no hidden diagnostic. Keep the existing hold only while its actual concentration and original deadlines permit; another genuine trigger occurrence may be considered. An already-spent release-round copy allowance alone is NOT a failed-release reason. At an exact governing expiry, expiry wins. Lost concentration, actual abandonment, successful replacement or another real ending terminates the hold without a refund; a failed release cannot restore a hold that ended.

On a valid release commitment, atomically consume this hold once and spend the real Reaction before resolving its one payload. No second RP/material payment, capture-use consumption, casting-family/Refrain update, cast hook or Counterspell window occurs. Subsequent prevention or a failed attack/save outcome does not refund the Reaction or preparation; actual source-specific hidden-eligibility checks retain their own paid timing. Duplicate callbacks/retry IDs cannot create a second payload or debit. Immediate Strike/Burst/Mend/Step end the held concentration after resolution. Ward/Hindrance/Boon continue the same one burden under their actual effect clock and earlier limits, never a second concentration slot.

OTHER USES AND PERSISTENCE. Another copy in the release round still needs its own genuinely available Action/source permission, current legal resources/credentials, its own new-commitment allowances and all ordinary concentration/cadence predicates. No Action, Reaction refresh, capture or second concentration slot is granted. A concentration-breaking new cast can end the old hold even though its allowance is irrelevant to the old release. Releasing a prior hold first leaves a genuinely free current-round allowance available for a separate lawful new commitment; a lawful prior current-round use does not by itself block the old hold's release. Actual competing-use opportunities before the owner's next regular START are illustrative prerequisites unless supplied by a real source; the old Ready cannot be carried past that START merely to obtain the ordinary Action. Save/load, extra turns, changing routes/profiles or round labels must preserve owner/hold identity, original expiry, actual consumed receipts, completed release identity and chronological/per-round ledgers. Release never rewrites a later cast's history. This rule is a proposed authoring successor, not implementation of scheduling, live perception, source-qualified recipient effects, canonical persistence or the game engine.

records.completeOperativeProcedure:
## Necrotic Affinity — Magic; Religion proficiency **or** character level8+

You have resistance to necrotic damage. Once per actual turn, when you hit with a melee attack, you may add1d6 necrotic damage. Natural/form melee attacks and off-turn Reaction attacks can qualify. A critical hit doubles this die to2d6; extra Actions in the same turn do not refresh it, while a genuinely different extra turn has its own entitlement. The die is feat damage, not spell damage.

Preserve the previously reviewed absorption procedure: when a legal necrotic spell/supernatural packet reaches the post-passive-defense stage, you may pay your Reaction to prevent `floor(post-defense necrotic damage /2)` before the old temporary-HP buffer. Resolve the remaining canonical damage once. Afterwards, if the holder remains living, offer temporary HP equal to the prevented amount until the end of the holder's next original regular turn, using its real endpoint marker. A1-point packet spends the Reaction but prevents/grants0. New temporary HP cannot absorb that same packet. Use `BufferLedger.necrotic_affinity` and `finish_necrotic_affinity`; do not apply resistance or damage twice.

When a creature actually dies from a canonical fatal damage/death root containing positive qualifying necrotic harm **owned by you**, attach a Necrotic Affinity seal to that death instance for24 elapsed hours. This includes your spells, the feat die, Agony Lance or another genuinely personal necrotic source. It is not limited to the feat's1d6. Supplying a summoned/transformed creature's statistics does not make its damage yours.

A mixed-type fatal root qualifies if your positive resolved necrotic component belongs to that root and the root actually causes death; no counterfactual subtraction test. Direct Instant Death, fatal death failures at0HP, or a later consequence expressly preserving that necrotic causal root can qualify. Temporary-HP-only absorption with no harmful consequence does not establish a seal.

The seal blocks applicable resurrection with an **actual spellRank/effectiveRank0..5**. Never invent a rank for unranked class features. Reviewed Paladin Grace Reversal is rank5 and is blocked; ordinary Resurrection7 and True Resurrection9 are above this restriction. Other resurrection requirements and Soul Bind still apply independently.

Same owner/death instance does not duplicate; different owners can have separate endpoints, but boolean blocking does not compound. A seal ends by elapsed expiry or an exact source able to remove that blocker, not generic cure. A legal return to life closes that death instance; its historical seals do not persist onto a later death. Transformations never create a new soul/body identity to evade a seal.

**NEW integration:** actual-turn identity, rank translation and fatal-root/death-instance bookkeeping. The broader printed necrotic-kill scope is preserved, correcting the narrower first draft.

## Soul Cage feat — Magic; level8+ and (Lifeleech **or** actual spellcasting ability)

On acquisition, lock one actually possessed spellcasting source/ability as this feat's DC provider. Agony uses that source's current normal spell-save DC. No freely switchable DC ability or general retraining is created.

**Shared Soul Charges:** each owner has one persistent pool0..3, shared with Lifeleech. A charge is a soul **spark/residue**, not custody of the whole soul. It neither prevents resurrection nor replaces/removes Soul Bind. The ordinary Soul Cage spell is a separate rank6/13RP spell awaiting its own operational review. Soulrender's separate whole-soul ritual unlock still requires actually binding the soul of a living named enemy; residue cannot satisfy it.

At an eligible hostile soul-bearing creature's actual death within30ft, with perception and legal line of effect, Soul Cage permits immediate optional capture with no Action or Reaction. A discrete physical black crystal must actually be possessed and available. Lifeleech collection is automatic and needs no crystal. Owning both never gives two charges for the same death.

Each owner permanently records the exact death event as evaluated, including ineligible events. There is no later corpse rescan after moving closer, gaining a feat/crystal or improving perception. For an eligible event, also reserve the immutable body for that owner's current completed-long-rest epoch. Declining or being at full capacity consumes that entitlement; there is no latent fourth charge. A new real death after resurrection is a new event, but the same body cannot supply the owner again in the same epoch. A future completed rest can permit a future new death, never the old corpse. Different owners evaluate independently.

Created/generated farming bodies and immutable object-origin transformed creatures are ineligible. Soul status otherwise follows actual source/canon or Director adjudication; this feat does not declare every undead/construct category soulless. Death/root/body identities persist through forms.

Charges live on the owner and do not decay automatically. Losing/destroying/transferring the crystal transfers or erases **zero** charges; Soul Cage capture/spending is unavailable without another actual legal black crystal. Another feat owner can use the transferred physical crystal for their own pool. There is no invented price, attunement, HP, durability or crystal charge capacity. During one uninterrupted quiet minute handling the crystal, you may voluntarily dissipate owned charges; this does nothing to any deceased soul.

**Shield:** Bonus Action; pay1 Soul Charge; one legal ally within30ft, including yourself; roll2d8 temporary HP with default lifetime. Pay before strongest-only comparison. An equal/stronger old shield does not refund the charge or Bonus Action.

**Agony Lance:** Action; pay2 Soul Charges; one perceived legal creature within60ft; CON save against the locked provider's current DC. Deal3d8 necrotic damage, half rounded down on success, then ordinary defenses/Core apply once. This is feat damage owned by you, not a spell, RP expenditure or spellcasting trigger.

The target also gains one **Agony healing-suppression family** record until the next committed ordinary HP-healing event with positive pre-reduction potential, or one elapsed minute. That next healing receives an exact×1/2 factor in the canonical healing pipeline. Save success or necrotic immunity affects damage but does not remove this separate rider. Multiple Agony Lances never multiply to1/4: a new paid application refreshes the single endpoint to `max(old expiry, new application+60s)` and retains contributor history.

Consume the suppression on the first applicable committed healing event even if a stronger arithmetic branch wins or actual healing is later capped/prohibited. Suppressed/inapplicable records do not apply or consume; absolute time continues. Temporary HP, stabilization, resurrection, prevention and maximum-HP changes are not ordinary HP healing and do not consume it. Removal requires an exact source capable of removing this magical suppression/debuff; generic cure is insufficient.

**NEW:** prerequisite parsing, residue identity, shared resource/death transaction, conduit role, activations/ranges/DC and the exact healing-suppression conversion. Original source IDs and relationships remain distinct.
